title: AI Product Video Generator for Demos | AIVideosUGC
description: Our AI product video generator shows your item in action, from a lid clicking shut to a lamp switching on. Make a short demo for Etsy, Shopify, or your ads.
h1: AI Product Video Generator for Showing How It Works
lead: Use an AI product video generator to plan a short demo around one visible action, such as a lid closing or a lamp switching on. Add a clear photo of that part and describe the movement you want to show.
intro: Product Videos focuses on one visible product action: a kettle pouring, a chair unfolding, or a drawer organizer holding cutlery. A focused demo can help shoppers understand how a feature works without turning one clip into a full tutorial.

With AIVideosUGC, upload a product photo and describe one action in a sentence. Pick the clip length and frame that suit the product action, from 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds and 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. It works well for home goods, kitchen tools, gadgets, bags, and other products where movement helps explain the feature.

benefits.d: A short clip of the lid opening or the light turning on explains more quickly than a list of specs.
Focused clips are easier to watch and easier to reuse. Make one for each feature and place them where they fit.
Choose 16:9 for a product page, 1:1 for listings, or 9:16 for YouTube Shorts, all from the same photo.

steps.d: Show the feature you want to demonstrate, such as a lid, latch, zipper or button, fully in frame. A clear phone image works.
Choose one clear action and where you plan to use the result.
Review the result with the real item, then describe the next feature as its own video.

faq.q: How is this different from image to video?
faq.a: Image to video adds requested camera movement to an existing still photo. A product demo focuses on one action, such as a zipper opening or a pump being pressed.

faq.q: Can I use the video on Etsy or Shopify?
faq.a: Yes. Etsy listing videos run 5 to 15 seconds, so make a 6, 10 or 15 second clip. On Shopify, add it to your product media the same way you add a photo.

faq.q: Will the video show my product accurately?
faq.a: Only describe actions your product can really do, and watch the clip before posting. If a button, color, or part looks different from the real item, make a new version rather than using that one.

faq.q: Can I add the price and product name?
faq.a: Add text later in Canva or CapCut. Letters generated by AI can come out garbled, so typed text is more reliable for names, prices, and dates.

faq.q: What actions work well for product videos?
faq.a: Show a clear operation such as opening, switching on, pouring, packing or fitting the product.

faq.q: Can I use a close-up operation shot?
faq.a: Yes. Close framing helps shoppers inspect a latch, button, lid, seam or other useful detail.

faq.q: Which aspect ratio should I choose for a product demo?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for TikTok or Shorts, 1:1 for a store feed, and 16:9 for a wide product page. Pick 10 or 15 seconds when the action needs a clear start and finish.

faq.q: How should I frame a moving part?
faq.a: Keep the full item and the moving part in focus before the action starts. Leave room around the edge, then let the lid, latch, zipper, pump or switch move once and stop.

overview.h2: Show one useful action, not a feature list
overview.p: Pick one thing a shopper would ask about (does the lid lock, how big is it inside) and make one short clip of it.

fit.h2: When a product demo is the right format
good: Home goods with a clear open, close, fold, pour, or switch action
Kitchen tools where the handoff or latch matters
Bags, organizers, and accessories with useful compartments
Listings that need one moving explanation beside still photos
not_ideal: Products whose value depends mainly on an exact printed claim
Actions that require a real person to explain results aloud

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. picker.title: Browse product ad formats
picker.lead: Choose a card by the moment a shopper needs to see, then adapt the product, hand position, and final hold to your own item. Creator reviews keep the product beside a face while a short line explains a benefit; hands-on demos stay close to the moving part; routines show how the item fits into a familiar task; taste reactions capture a first sip or bite. Each prompt is one operation, with no invented logo or packaging. Use the preview to check that the action, color, and ending frame match what you sell.

uses.h: Show the item, then its feature
uses.d: A product page needs a clear action that answers one question: what does this item do? Use a wide or square frame to show the item first, then the mechanism in close view. A lid, latch, zipper, pump, or switch should move once and stop clearly. Keep a hand in frame when scale matters, and leave enough space around the product for the page layout. After download, compare the clip with the real item before publishing; an altered button or cap is a reason to make another version.

uses.h: Add a product clip to a listing
uses.d: Short ads work when the feature is visible before the viewer scrolls. Use a vertical framing for a creator review, a taste reaction, or a quick try-on; use a product-level angle for a cable connection or a close operation. Plan one sound that supports the movement, such as a click, pour, zip, or brush pass. Add a typed price or headline later in your editor so the product scene stays clean and the spelling stays correct.

visual.overview: A product demo shows one useful action from the first frame to the last: a dropper lifting, a cap clicking shut, a cable connecting, a brush catching fur, or a shoe tightening before a walk. Start with a complete photo, name one movement, and keep the item stable so shoppers can judge the feature. Use [how-to video templates](/ai-video-generation/how-to-video) for numbered steps, [UGC ad videos](/ai-video-generation/ugc-ad-video) for a first-person review, or [image to video](/ai-video-generation/image-to-video) when the still only needs camera movement. Choose the placement before you write: vertical for [TikTok](/platforms/tiktok-ads) or Shorts, wide for a product page, and square for a store feed.
